Outcomes
The primary outcome was a composite of worsening heart failure, defined as either an unplanned hospitalization or an
urgent visit requiring intravenous therapy for heart failure, or cardiovascular death. The primary outcome was analyzed
concurrently in both the full population and in patients with LVEF < 60% with alpha split between these analyses. The
dual primary analyses were introduced in a protocol amendment on November 4, 2020. Secondary objectives were to
determine whether dapagliflozin was superior to placebo in reducing the total number of worsening heart failure events
(hospitalization for heart failure and urgent heart failure visits) and cardiovascular death in the full study population and
the sub-population with LVEF < 60%, in improving patient-reported outcomes measured by the Kansas City
Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) total symptom score (TSS) (scores range from 0 to 100, with higher scores
indicating fewer symptoms and physical limitations), in reducing cardiovascular death, and in reducing all-cause
mortality. The primary KCCQ-TSS analysis was changed in the statistical analysis plan on November 6th, 2020 to include
only patients who had their 8-month assessment planned or performed before March 11, 2020. All potential primary
events were adjudicated by an independent clinical events committee blinded to treatment assignment based on
prespecified criteria2.
In light of the prior extensive safety data regarding dapagliflozin, only collection of serious adverse events and adverse
events leading to discontinuation were required. Additionally, events related to volume depletion, major hypoglycemic
events, diabetic ketoacidosis, amputation, and renal adverse events were collected.


General Statistical Considerations
The dual primary analyses (time to first occurrence of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure) were conducted
concurrently in the overall population and in patients with a LVEF < 60% (See below and Figure S1). Accounting for one
interim analysis, the total alpha used in the final analysis was 0.048, with 0.024 allocated to the analysis of the full
population, and 0.038 allocated to the analysis of patients with an LVEF < 60% (see below for details). Other than the
unblinded statisticians and programmers at the independent statistics group, Statistics Collaborative Inc., performing the
analysis for the Data Monitoring Committee, no one, either at the sponsor or academic leadership, was unblinded for
the interim analysis or knew the results other than the recommendation to continue the trial. A sample size of 6100
patients followed for at least 13.5 and up to 39 months was estimated to provide 1117 events, resulting in 93% power to
detect a 20% relative risk reduction for the primary endpoint in the full population with a two-sided alpha of 0.024. The
relative risk reduction was based on data from the EMPAREG Outcomes trial3. We included data from all patients who

19|BACKGROUND
20|Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce the risk of hospitaliza-
21|tion for heart failure and cardiovascular death among patients with chronic heart
22|failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less. Whether SGLT2 in-
23|hibitors are effective in patients with a higher left ventricular ejection fraction
24|remains less certain.
25|METHODS
26|We randomly assigned 6263 patients with heart failure and a left ventricular ejec-
27|tion fraction of more than 40% to receive dapagliflozin (at a dose of 10 mg once
28|daily) or matching placebo, in addition to usual therapy. The primary outcome was
29|a composite of worsening heart failure (which was defined as either an unplanned
30|hospitalization for heart failure or an urgent visit for heart failure) or cardiovas-
31|cular death, as assessed in a time-to-event analysis.
32|RESULTS
33|Over a median of 2.3 years, the primary outcome occurred in 512 of 3131 patients
34|(16.4%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 610 of 3132 patients (19.5%) in the pla-
35|cebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.92; P<0.001).
36|Worsening heart failure occurred in 368 patients (11.8%) in the dapagliflozin
37|group and in 455 patients (14.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95%
38|CI, 0.69 to 0.91); cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261
39|patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05). Total events
40|and symptom burden were lower in the dapagliflozin group than in the placebo
41|group. Results were similar among patients with a left ventricular ejection fraction
42|of 60% or more and those with a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 60%,
43|and results were similar in prespecified subgroups, including patients with or
44|without diabetes. The incidence of adverse events was similar in the two groups.
45|CONCLUSIONS
46|Dapagliflozin reduced the combined risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovas-
47|cular death among patients with heart failure and a mildly reduced or preserved
48|ejection fraction. (Funded by AstraZeneca; DELIVER ClinicalTrials.gov number,
49|NCT03619213.)
